💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scientific and satellite findings warn of widespread contamination in Gaza, posing grave threats to public health ‘for generations to come’.
  • Israel’s destruction of Gaza has left a devastating environmental legacy with poisoned water, contaminated soil and toxic air threatening the life-support systems that the population depends on for survival, according to a report.
  • Israel’s military assault has created widespread contamination across the entire strip, the report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (Ceobs) finds, with heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, and sewage making the air, soil and water dangerous for Palestinians for decades to come.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scientific and satellite findings warn of widespread contamination in Gaza, posing grave threats to public health ‘for generations to come’.

Israel’s destruction of Gaza has left a devastating environmental legacy with poisoned water, contaminated soil and toxic air threatening the life-support systems that the population depends on for survival, according to a report.

Israel’s military assault has created widespread contamination across the entire strip, the report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (Ceobs) finds, with heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, and sewage making the air, soil and water dangerous for Palestinians for decades to come.

Oxfam International’s executive director, Amitabh Behar, noted: “Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza includes military assaults on its environment, which are environmental war crimes threatening life now and for generations to come.”.

He said the “destruction and contamination of Gaza” have “fundamentally degraded the environmental conditions necessary for human safety and survival” and breach Israel’s legal obligations under international humanitarian and human rights law.

Sources indicate that “Palestinians living in Gaza are being exposed to toxins … through air, food, water and via direct contact with contaminated soils and debris. These risks will persist for generations to come, unless clean-up, remediation and recovery actions are prioritised.”.

In 2025 and earlier this year, the UN independent international commission of inquiry found that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza and that Israeli officials, including the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, incited these acts. The Israeli mission in Geneva said Israel rejected the commission’s “libellous sham”. Netanyahu is separately wanted by the international criminal court (ICC) for war crimes.

Oxfam’s report gives the most comprehensive picture to date of what it calls the “toxic wasteland” created by the Israeli assault which has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians and wounded at least 175,000, while thousands still remain unaccounted for under the rubble.

Using satellite imagery, remote sensing, scientific analysis and other open-source data, it concludes contamination in Gaza is “widespread, severe and consequential, with serious implications for public health and civilian survival”.

Behar mentioned: “It is horrifying to begin to understand the extent of toxic contamination being faced by the population, who can neither escape nor protect themselves properly from the dangers. In an area as small, oppressed and densely populated as Gaza, continuous exposure is inevitable, with people surrounded by waste and sewage, spreading pests and the risk of disease growing.

“Raw sewage is pouring into the sea and leaking into the ground, while the destruction of Gaza’s sanitation systems leaves people with little protection from the contamination around them.”.

He added the “associated health consequences will be severe, with children and pregnant women among those facing the highest risks”.

The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) estimates that Israel’s military operations have generated more than 61m tonnes of debris across the territory, turning Gaza’s destroyed homes, neighbourhoods and infrastructure into a vast reservoir of potentially hazardous materials.

The report’s author, Lama Abdul Samad, a global water and sanitation specialist at Oxfam, said tackling the environmental damage in Gaza will be “highly challenging because contamination is dispersed across the urban rubble, farmland, water systems and soils, while unexploded ordnance continues to restrict safe access to most areas”.

“The analysis highlights the urgent need for Israel to grant access for a detailed environmental assessment on the ground to clarify the risks to public health and identify options for urgent harm-reduction measures. Restoration is likely to require extensive clearance, monitoring and specialised remediation of affected areas from contaminants such as explosive residues, organic pollutants and heavy metals.”.

Behar said that as international attention increasingly turned to Gaza’s reconstruction, environmental recovery must not be treated as an afterthought, but as a vital undertaking in parallel.

“Rebuilding Gaza without simultaneously understanding and addressing the extent of environmental contamination risks creating long-term public health consequences for generations to come,” he said.

The Israeli government has been contacted for comment.

#127604. Latest Update: Hundreds of millions at risk from Chinese shopping app malware

📅 02 Apr 2023 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1920 w)

General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNN ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Hundreds of millions at risk from Chinese shopping app malware

📅 02 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1920 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It is one of China’s most popular shopping apps, selling clothing, groceries and just about everything else under the sun to more than 750 million consumers a month.
  • But according to cybersecurity researchers, it can also bypass users’ cell phone security to monitor activities on other apps, check notifications, read private messages and change settings.
  • While many apps collect vast troves of user data, sometimes without explicit consent, experts say e-commerce giant Pinduoduo has taken violations of privacy and data security to the next level.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is one of China’s most popular shopping apps, selling clothing, groceries and just about everything else under the sun to more than 750 million consumers a month.

But according to cybersecurity researchers, it can also bypass users’ cell phone security to monitor activities on other apps, check notifications, read private messages and change settings.

And once installed, it’s tough to remove.

While many apps collect vast troves of user data, sometimes without explicit consent, experts say e-commerce giant Pinduoduo has taken violations of privacy and data security to the next level.

In a detailed investigation, CNN spoke to half a dozen cybersecurity teams from Asia, Europe and the United States — as well as multiple former and current Pinduoduo employees — after receiving a tipoff.

Multiple experts identified the presence of malware on the Pinduoduo app that exploited vulnerabilities in Android operating systems. Firm insiders mentioned the exploits were utilized to spy on users and competitors, allegedly to boost sales.

“We haven’t seen a mainstream app like this trying to escalate their privileges to gain access to things that they’re not supposed to gain access to,” remarked Mikko Hyppönen, chief research officer at WithSecure, a Finnish cybersecurity firm.

“This is highly unusual, and it is pretty damning for Pinduoduo.”.

Malware, short for malicious software, refers to any software developed to steal data or interfere with computer systems and mobile devices.

Evidence of sophisticated malware in the Pinduoduo app comes amid intense scrutiny of Chinese-developed apps like TikTok over concerns about data security.

Some American lawmakers are pushing for a national ban on the popular short-video app, whose CEO Shou Chew was grilled by Congress for five hours last week about its relations with the Chinese government.

Recent findings suggest that the revelations are also likely to draw more attention to Pinduoduo’s international sister app, Temu, which is topping US download charts and fast expanding in other Western markets. Both are owned by Nasdaq-listed PDD, a multinational firm with roots in China.

While Temu has not been implicated, Pinduoduo’s alleged actions risk casting a shadow over its sister app’s global expansion.

It has been revealed that there is no evidence that Pinduoduo has handed data to the Chinese government. But as Beijing enjoys significant leverage over businesses under its jurisdiction, there are concerns from US lawmakers that any manufacturer operating in China could be forced to cooperate with a broad range of security activities.

The findings follow Google’s suspension of Pinduoduo from its Play Store in March, citing malware identified in versions of the app.

An ensuing report from Bloomberg remarked a Russian cybersecurity firm had also identified potential malware in the app.

Pinduoduo has previously rejected “the speculation and accusation that Pinduoduo app is malicious.”.

CNN has contacted PDD multiple times over email and phone for comment, but has not received a response.

Pinduoduo, which boasts a user base that accounts for three quarters of China’s online population and a market value three times that of eBay (EBAY), wasn’t always an online shopping behemoth.

Founded in 2015 in Shanghai by Colin Huang, a former Google employee, the startup was fighting to establish itself in a market long dominated by e-commerce stalwarts Alibaba (BABA) and JD.com (JD).

It succeeded by offering steep discounts on friends-and-family group buying orders and focusing on lower-income rural areas.

According to recent reports, pinduoduo posted triple digit growth in monthly owners until the end of 2018, the year it listed in Latest York. By the middle of 2020, though, the increase in monthly users had slowed to around 50% and would continue to decline, according to its earnings reports.

It was in 2020, according to a current Pinduoduo employee, that the company set up a team of about 100 engineers and product managers to dig for vulnerabilities in Android phones, develop ways to exploit them — and turn that into profit.

According to the source, who requested anonymity for fear of reprisals, the company only targeted users in rural areas and smaller towns initially, while avoiding users in megacities such as Beijing and Shanghai.

“The goal was to reduce the risk of being exposed,” they mentioned.

By collecting expansive data on user activities, the tech giant was able to create a comprehensive portrait of people’ habits, interests and preferences, according to the source.

This allowed it to improve its machine learning model to offer more personalized push notifications and ads, attracting users to open the app and place orders, they mentioned.

The team was disbanded in early March, the source added, after questions about their activities came to light.

PDD didn’t reply to CNN’s repeated requests for comment on the team.

Approached by CNN, researchers from Tel Aviv-based cyber firm Check Point Research, Delaware-based app security startup Oversecured and Hyppönen’s WithSecure conducted independent analysis of the 6.49.0 version of the app, released on Chinese app stores in late February.

Recent findings suggest that google Play is not available in China, and Android consumers in the country download their apps from local stores. In March, when Google suspended Pinduoduo, it said it had found malware in off-Play versions of the app.

The researchers found code designed to achieve “privilege escalation”: a type of cyberattack that exploits a vulnerable operating system to gain a higher level of access to data than it’s supposed to have, according to experts.

“Our team has reverse engineered that code and we can confirm that it tries to escalate rights, tries to gain access to things normal apps wouldn’t be able to do on Android phones,” noted Hyppönen.

The app was able to continue running in the background and prevent itself from being uninstalled, which allowed it to boost its monthly active user rates, Hyppönen remarked. It also had the ability to spy on competitors by tracking activity on other shopping apps and getting information from them, he added.

Check Point Research additionally identified ways in which the app was able to evade scrutiny.

The app deployed a method that allowed it to push updates without an app store review process meant to detect malicious applications, the researchers said.

They also identified in some plug-ins the intent to obscure potentially malicious components by hiding them under legitimate file names, such as Google’s.

“Such a technique is widely used by malware developers that inject malicious code into applications that have legitimate functionality,” they said.

In China, about three quarters of smartphone people are on the Android system. Apple (AAPL)’s iPhone has 25% market share, according to Daniel Ives of Wedbush Securities.

Sergey Toshin, the founder of Oversecured, remarked Pinduoduo’s malware specifically targeted different Android-based operating systems, including those used by Samsung, Huawei, Xiaomi and Oppo.

CNN has reached out to these companies for comment.

Toshin described Pinduoduo as “the most dangerous malware” ever found among mainstream apps.

Industry observers note that “I’ve never seen anything like this before. It’s like, super expansive,” he said.

Most phone manufacturers globally customize the core Android software, the Android Open Source Project (AOSP), to add unique features and applications to their own devices.

Toshin found Pinduoduo to have exploited about 50 Android system vulnerabilities. Most of the exploits were tailor made for customized parts known as the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) code, which tends to be audited less often than AOSP and is therefore more prone to vulnerabilities, he said.

Pinduoduo also exploited a number of AOSP vulnerabilities, including one which was flagged by Toshin to Google in February 2022. Google fixed the bug this March, he remarked.

According to Toshin, the exploits allowed Pinduoduo access to consumers’ locations, contacts, calendars, notifications and photo albums without their consent. They were also able to change system settings and access users’ social network accounts and chats, he mentioned.

In a recent development, of the six teams CNN spoke to for this story, three did not conduct full examinations. But their primary reviews showed that Pinduoduo asked for a large number of permissions beyond the normal functions of a shopping app.

They included “potentially invasive permissions” such as “set wallpaper” and “download without notification,” mentioned René Mayrhofer, head of the Institute of Networks and Security at the Johannes Kepler University Linz in Austria.

Suspicions about malware in Pinduoduo’s app were first raised in late February in a report by a Chinese cybersecurity firm called Dark Navy. Even though the analysis didn’t directly name the shopping giant, the report spread promptly among other researchers, who did name the manufacturer. Some of the analysts followed up with their own reports confirming the original findings.

Soon after, on March 5, Pinduoduo issued a fresh enhancement of its app, version 6.50.0, which removed the exploits, according to two experts who CNN spoke to.

Two days after the enhancement, Pinduoduo disbanded the team of engineers and product managers who had developed the exploits, according to the Pinduoduo source.

The next day, team members found themselves locked out of Pinduoduo’s bespoke workplace communication app, Knock, and lost access to files on the firm’s internal network. Engineers also found their access to substantial data, data sheets and the log system revoked, the source stated.

According to recent reports, most of the team were transferred to work at Temu. They were assigned to different departments at the subsidiary, with some working on marketing or developing push notifications, according to the source.

A core group of about 20 cybersecurity engineers who specialize in finding and exploiting vulnerabilities remain at Pinduoduo, they remarked.

Toshin of Oversecured, who looked into the revision, said although the exploits were removed, the underlying code was still there and could be reactivated to carry out attacks.

Pinduoduo has been able to grow its user base against a backdrop of the Chinese government’s regulatory clampdown on Significant Tech that began in late 2020.

That year, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology debuted a sweeping crackdown on apps that illegally collect and use personal data.

In 2021, Beijing passed its first comprehensive data privacy legislation.

The Personal Information Protection Law stipulates that no party should illegally collect, process or transmit personal information. They’re also banned from exploiting internet-related security vulnerabilities or engaging in actions that endanger cybersecurity.

Pinduoduo’s apparent malware would be a violation of those laws, tech policy experts say, and should have been detected by the regulator.

Sources indicate that “This would be embarrassing for the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, because this is their job,” stated Kendra Schaefer, a tech policy expert at Trivium China, a consultancy. “They’re supposed to check Pinduoduo, and the fact that they didn’t find (anything) is embarrassing for the regulator.”.

Recent findings suggest that the ministry has regularly published lists to name and shame apps found to have undermined user privacy or other rights. It also publishes a separate list of apps that are removed from app stores for failing to comply with regulations.

Pinduoduo did not appear on any of the lists.

CNN has reached out to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and the Cyberspace Administration of China for comment.

On Chinese social media, some cybersecurity experts questioned why regulators haven’t taken any action.

“Probably none of our regulators can understand coding and programming, nor do they understand technology. You can’t even understand the malicious code when it’s shoved right in front of your face,” a cybersecurity expert with 1.8 million followers wrote last week in a viral post on Weibo, a Twitter-like platform.

The post was censored the next day.

CNN’s Kristie Lu Stout and Sean Lyngaas contributed reporting.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Indonesian rescue teams are searching for 37 workers who remained unaccounted for after a fire at a candy-making factory killed at least three people, officials said on Sunday.
  • The fire occurred at the Fonusa Agung Mulia factory on Java, around 50 kilometers (31 miles) west of the capital, Jakarta.
  • Footage from the scene showed workers' family members waiting for news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Indonesian rescue teams are searching for 37 workers who remained unaccounted for after a fire at a candy-making factory killed at least three people, officials said on Sunday.

The fire occurred at the Fonusa Agung Mulia factory on Java, around 50 kilometers (31 miles) west of the capital, Jakarta.

Footage from the scene showed workers' family members waiting for news.

The factory caught fire on Saturday afternoon, local search and rescue agency official Rizky Dwianto remarked.

"All elements of the joint SAR (search-and-rescue) team are making maximum effort to locate the victims while prioritizing the safety of personnel in the field," he added.

Rizky mentioned four people injured in the blaze had been taken to a nearby hospital and health clinic. Eleven more were said to have been rescued alive, with dozens of others still missing.

The authorities deployed 15 fire trucks to the scene, along with a rescue team including the police, the military, the Red Cross and volunteers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Authorities noted the blaze had largely been contained as of Sunday. However, firefighters were still carrying out intensive cooling operations to allow access all parts of the factory, according to Tubagus Mahfud, the operations chief of the district fire department.

He noted there were still hot spots in some parts of the building.

Sources indicate that "We are conducting sweeps in the areas that have already been brought under control," Mahfud noted. "Parts of the structure had collapsed, while poor lighting conditions required firefighters to proceed cautiously.".

Drone footage highlights the fire destroyed large sections of the three-story building, bringing down the roof in some places.

Survivors said the fire started in a cooling unit on the third floor.

Recent findings suggest that the exact death toll was not immediately clear. While three people were confirmed to be dead, a report by the Reuters news agency indicated police removed 24 body bags from the scene.

Separately, the manufacturer's CEO mentioned around 300 people were on site on Saturday, with 65 workers believed to be in the affected area when the fire broke out.

Senior police official in charge of victims' identification, Wahyu Hidayati Dwi Palupi, urged family members to provide DNA samples and other information to identify the victims, warning that the victims' condition made visual identification impossible.

The factory, located in the Serang district of Banten province, produces Milkita, an Indonesian brand of milk-based candies and snack products exported to over 40 countries worldwide.

The blaze marks only the latest in Indonesia's series of deadly industrial fires in recent years, raising questions about the country's workplace safety standards.

Among other disasters, at least 22 people were killed in a fire last December that broke out in a seven-story building in Jakarta after a suspected drone battery explosion, police stated.

An explosion in a nickel-processing plant in the east of the country killed at least 13 people in 2023.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Considering the current state of affairs, the best gifts for the women in our lives are the ones that let them mentally clock out for a bit. The world is on fire—literally and figuratively. Plastic is melting onto corals, the measles are back, and just to kick us while we’re down, the girlies can’t even enjoy a Caesar salad or some chips and guac in peace. Some days, I'll catch myself staring at the sky and think, I wish I could hitch a ride to space, but of course, Elon Musk has ruined that fantasy for me, too.

If the woman in your life is exhausted by the headlines, by the slow-motion collapse of democracy, by the sheer audacity of men in power, or perhaps just the overall state of humanity, she deserves a treat. She frankly needs a portal to another reality, but since that's not possible just yet, a temporary escape will have to do.

Here are the best gifts for women surviving the dystopian quest that is 2026. For more thoughtful gift ideas for women, check out Gifts for Moms, Best Graduation Gifts, and Best Stocking Stuffers.

She’s been carrying the weight of the world for far too long. Therabody’s ThermBack LED melts away tension with targeted heat, vibration, LED, and far-infrared therapies. With three heat levels (up to 113 degrees Fahrenheit) and three vibration patterns (low, high, and wave), it stimulates circulation, loosens tight muscles in the lower back, and offers relief when she’s sitting at her desk for eight hours trying not to scream. It also doubles as a soothing heat pad for period cramps. Best of all, it automatically shuts off, so she doesn’t have to worry about turning it off. Check out some other options in our guide to the Best Massagers.

When in doubt, perfume makes a lovely gift. A beautifully bottled eau de parfum inherently feels luxurious, but fragrance is a personal territory, so it’s best to avoid anything too polarizing unless you know her tastes. One safe and elegant bet: Bulgari’s Omnia Amethyste Eau de Parfum. Its soft, floral-woody scent is pleasant to wear year-round on its own or layer with her existing favorites. The composition opens with iris petal and ambrette accords, blooms into iris absolute and Damask rose, then settles into a warm, earthy base of bourbon vanilla and cistus labdanum absolute.

Sources indicate that women are expected to do it all, so why shouldn’t their alarm clocks? The Hatch Sleep Clock is a multitasking marvel. Along with being one of the best sunrise clocks on the market, it’s also a dimmable bedside light, a sound machine, and the first Hatch device to offer contactless sleep tracking. That last bit means she can monitor her slumber without strapping yet another gadget to her body. To unlock Hatch’s full audio library, she’ll need a Hatch+ membership ($6 per month), so I'd spring for at least three months. Consider it an investment in everyone’s well-being when she’s finally getting her beauty sleep.

I absolutely adore Quince’s Mongolian cashmere collection. The Oversized Boyfriend Cardigan is the ultimate wardrobe staple for three out of four seasons. It’s not just perfect for sweata-weatha fall; it’s also cozy for rainy spring days and during the chill of winter. The fisherman rib detailing is uber-coastal, a charming touch to an already flattering and versatile piece. If your giftee is more of a sweatshirt gal, you also can't go wrong with the Fisherman Pullover Hoodie ($120) or the Full-Zip Hoodie ($120).

According to recent reports, everyone and their mother has an LED mask these days. If the woman in your life doesn’t, congratulations: You’ve found her gift. Chances are the Shark CryoGlow LED Face Mask is already on her wishlist. And if it isn't, she simply hasn’t done enough research. The CryoGlow delivers red, infrared, and blue light, which is everything your face could possibly need short of a dermatologist. Its preset routines live on an attached controller, so there’s no troubleshooting. The real selling point, though, is the under-eye cooling pads, which help reduce puffiness and add a therapeutic element to the experience. I gifted one to my mother, and now she has to actively defend it from her friends.

Get her the Eva Wearable Vibrator. A hands-free clitoral stimulation toy that can be used solo, but is best during penetrative sex. It’s tiny. It’s mighty. It’s hands-free (!!!), made of soft silicone, with three intensity levels. Gift the Eva to your best friend, or to your partner if you want to spice things up, in which case, you’re welcome.

Industry observers note that if I have to feed myself, I want a kitchen appliance that does most of my labor. The Breville Smart Oven Air Fryer Noir is that appliance. She’s goth. She’s gorgeous. She air-fries, slow-cooks, and bakes with zero complaints. There are 11 preset functions, to be exact. I don’t know what all of them do, and I don’t care, because she knows. I don’t want to think about settings, and with Breville’s Element iQ system, which auto-adjusts temperature for precision cooking, I don’t have to. There’s even an app, which I didn’t download because I’m busy. You can check out more of our Air Fryer picks here.

In a recent development, if she already owns an LED mask, it’s time to give her scalp the same VIP treatment. Red-light therapy isn’t just for pattern baldness; it may also help women experiencing all types of hair thinning and shedding, including postpartum hair loss. It can also help calm the scalp, increase blood flow, and regulate oil production. Reviewer Nena Farrell loves the HigherDose Red Light Hat, which is relatively affordable compared with competitors and looks like an ordinary baseball cap. That means she can take her self-care outside, and no one would ever know. How would they know?

If she’s training for a marathon, tracking her stress cycles, or just wants hard data to justify why she feels like garbage, the Oura Ring 5 is the most stylish health tracker out there. Packed with advanced sensors, it monitors heart rate, skin temperature, sleep quality, and stress levels. It's also one of the only wearables that can reliably predict my menstrual cycle. Plus, it works with both Android and iOS, so she’s not locked into a single tech ecosystem.

Recent findings suggest that the BrüMate Togosa gets it. It’s a wine chiller, pitcher, or whatever you need it to be because we no longer have the patience for single-purpose objects. Slide in a prechilled bottle, twist the lid shut, and let the BevGuard triple insulation keep your drink icy without ice, condensation, or a watery demise. When the vibe shifts from pinot to sangria, swap out the chiller lid and pour in your batch of whatever (up to 49 ounces). The leakproof strainer lid also keeps fruit, ice, and other garnishes from pouring through. And because being checked out of Earth doesn’t mean trashing it, its lids are made from 13 recycled water bottles, some finishes are dishwasher-safe to conserve water usage, and the vessel itself is built to last a lifetime. (If for some reason it doesn’t, BrüMate also offers a lifetime warranty.).

She may not be able to move to another planet, but she can build a 3D model of the Milky Way from the comfort of her home. This 3,000-ish piece LEGO set recreates the spiral galaxy, turning our jumbled universe into galactic home decor. The finished piece can be mounted on the wall as a daily reminder that Earth is just one of billions of planets we believe exist—surely, at least one of them has better men.

Recent findings suggest that the Everywhere Tote is for the woman who is going where the universe takes her. It has everything one might need for far-flung travels: a 16-inch padded laptop sleeve, a handful of interior pockets, and a water-resistant nylon exterior for when you’re caught in an otherworldly atmospheric anomaly. Available in elemental shades like coast blue, sea green, and clay pink—it’s at home anywhere, from the gym to an impromptu odyssey. If she needs to jet off on a moment’s notice, it’s got a key clip, a trolley sleeve, and an exterior pocket for her wallet and passport. It also meets airlines’ personal item requirements.

Sometimes, the only way to check out is to beam yourself into another world, preferably one with juicier plotlines. This projector has 450 ISO lumens and 1080p resolution, with 4K support and color calibration. The gimbal stand tilts 165 degrees for projecting on walls, ceilings, or the back of an RV. The included hard-shell case is great for portability and easy storage. It runs for 2.5 hours on a single charge, and it's power bank-compatible, so you can watch from anywhere. Its AI-powered setup takes care of autofocus, screen fit, obstacle avoidance, and keystone correction, so she doesn't have to fiddle with settings with every tectonic shake. For more projectors, check out our guide.

Cozy Earth’s Bamboo Pajama Set is one of my favorite sets to wear on a lazy Sunday. The button-up pocketed design features chic contrast piping that lends a hotel-style aesthetic. They make me want to put on my LED mask, pick up my Kindle, and sip on sleepy girl mocktails until I doze off. Made from 95 percent bamboo viscose and 5 percent spandex, this knit blend is cooler and more breathable than cotton. Cozy Earth introduces new colors and prints each season, though the lighter shades can be somewhat sheer. If your giftee is over 5 foot 7 inches, I recommend the tall inseam. Sizes range from XXS to XXXL.

These Speks Odds Silicone Fidget Magnets are here to help you survive your stay in the stress-stricken simulation. Each set comes with three palm-sized magnets, encased in soft, textured silicone, designed to keep your hands busy while your brain zones out. I can’t stop fiddling with them when I’m watching TV and during Zoom calls. I can’t risk losing them by taking them outside, so they’ve found a home on my desk.

Speks also sells starter kits and gift bundles packed with other fidget toys. I loved the Moon Jelly Gump Memory Gel Stress Ball, until I handed it to my boyfriend for five minutes and he popped it. Men ruin everything.

Sources indicate that walking home alone at night on this planet is an absolute nightmare. If she can’t teleport away from creeps, she can at least blast a 130-decibel siren and flashing strobe light in their direction. The Birdie is a small but mighty alarm that will (hopefully) deter attackers and alert anyone nearby for help.

I’ve used the original model for over a year (see my thoughts in my guide to the Best Personal Safety Alarms), and it’s given me peace of mind whenever I’m walking solo. The Birdie+, which I have yet to test, adds some useful features like location sharing, emergency support, and even a fake call function for a quick exit strategy. Plus, it comes in the cutest patterns. My one caveat is that this wouldn't be my first choice for a birthday gift or Valentine's Day, as it's kind of a downer.

She’s carrying her team at work, her family, and the knowledge that a recession is potentially looming. Don’t make her carry her water bottle, too. WanderFull’s Hydrobags have a thick, comfortable strap that takes a little bit of the load off her shoulders and come in dozens of colors and materials (including a upcoming clear stadium line), one of which is sure to match her vibe. All Hydrobags bags can hold any handle-less water bottle up to 11 inches tall and 3.5 inches in diameter and sport two pockets for her phone and cards. If you can’t redistribute the household labor, the least you could do is redistribute the weight of her emotional-support beverage. —Kat Merck.

#127600. Best Laptops for Travel (2026): Which to Take on the Road

Best Laptops for Travel (2026): Which to Take on the Road

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2090 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a laptop reviewer, I have plenty of devices to choose from when I travel for work.
  • Fortunately, there are many great travel laptops, and you’ll still appreciate them when you aren’t on the road.
  • Industry observers note that if there’s an obvious pick for the best travel laptop, it’s the Dell XPS 13.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a laptop reviewer, I have plenty of devices to choose from when I travel for work. In some cases, my favorite overall laptop doesn’t translate into the one I want to travel with. When I’m squeezed into a plane, I’ll choose maximum battery life and portability over features like a bigger screen or more ports.

Fortunately, there are many great travel laptops, and you’ll still appreciate them when you aren’t on the road. Of the hundreds of laptops I’ve tested in my life, here are the ones I always choose to travel with.

Industry observers note that if there’s an obvious pick for the best travel laptop, it’s the Dell XPS 13. It’s been the best compact laptop you can buy for years, and that’s even more true in its latest incarnation. The key dimension to pay attention to on the XPS 13 is the depth, which is crucial for air travel. At 7.9 inches, it’s among the smallest laptops you can buy. Those economy-class seat-back tray tables on airplanes are only around 10 inches deep, and while that’s technically enough to accommodate even a 16-inch MacBook Pro, whether you can actually open the lid and use the laptop is another question. The XPS 13 is even smaller than the MacBook Neo, despite having a larger screen.

Industry observers note that the XPS 13 achieves this by using a 13.4-inch display (measured diagonally), compared to many of the 14-inch laptops on this list. Second, it has very narrow bezels around that screen, minimizing the device’s overall footprint. While 14-inch laptops have become more popular in recent years, that bigger display size also increases the overall footprint—and every millimeter counts when working on a plane. The XPS 13 still has enough room for your palms when typing (unless you have huge hands), and the keyboard is among my favorites to type on.

In a recent development, the other two major advantages for travel are weight and battery life. This little laptop only weighs 2.2 pounds, a full half-pound lighter than the 13-inch MacBook Air. You might forget you have it in your backpack while traveling.

In a recent development, now, the XPS 13 isn't the most powerful laptop in the world—at least not the cheaper models. The standard version comes with only 8 GB of RAM and an Intel chip with only two Performance cores. It’s good enough for basic web tasks, but for real work, you might run into limitations. You can address this by opting for the 16 GB model (which keeps the price under $1,000) or upgrading to the much more powerful Core Ultra 7 355 processor. The latter is much more expensive and comes with twice the storage, but it doesn’t add extra weight or size. Regardless of the chip you choose, the XPS 13 gets absolutely fantastic battery life. It depends on what you're doing with it, but you could easily work through a long international flight without worrying about plugging in.

Sources indicate that if weight is your primary concern, the Asus Zenbook A14 is another contender. Despite being larger overall than the XPS 13 (with a bigger screen), the Zenbook A14 weighs 2.16 pounds—a hair lighter than the Dell. That’s seriously impressive, and I still remember how astounded I was when I first picked it up. Asus debuts its “ceraluminum” material in the chassis, which gives you the sturdiness of aluminum with the lightness of plastic. It’s not quite as rigid as metal, but it’s not as flimsy as ultra-light laptops in the past.

In a recent development, if you’re less worried about working on the plane and more about lugging a laptop around, the Zenbook A14 is a good choice. The Zenbook A14 has several advantages over the XPS 13 that can be helpful on the go, including built-in ports like a headphone jack, USB-A, and HDMI. If you’re working out of a remote office or presenting to a client, these can definitely come in handy. The XPS 13 only has two USB-C ports and nothing else.

Recent findings suggest that there are a number of different versions of the Asus Zenbook A14 floating around out there. I’d stay away from the 8 GB model Asus sells and opt for the 16 GB model instead. There’s also a newer model that uses the Snapdragon X2 Elite chip, but I don’t think it’s worth the extra $450—especially not for a laptop focused on travel.

The 13-inch MacBook Air also makes a great travel laptop. It’s relatively small, thanks to its 13.6-inch screen.

In terms of portability, its main advantage over the XPS 13 and Zenbook A14 is its thinness. At 0.42 inches, it’s the thinnest laptop out there—and it doesn’t stick huge rubber feet on the bottom to compensate like other laptops do, such as the Razer Blade 14. You might not think thickness matters much in a travel laptop, but if you’re squeezing stuff into a backpack, every extra millimeter matters.

The MacBook Neo is also worth mentioning here. It’s not quite as thin as the MacBook Air, but because its screen is 0.4 inches smaller, it has a more compact overall footprint. Battery life is the bigger problem when taking the Neo on a trip, as it doesn’t last as long as the MacBook Air or Dell XPS 13. The 8 GB of RAM limitation doesn’t affect its use as a travel laptop much, but it's something to consider for a work laptop in general. That said, it has a very pretty screen for a laptop at this price.

According to recent reports, budget laptops aren’t typically known for being particularly lightweight and travel-worthy. Most of them struggle, especially with battery life. The HP OmniBook 5 might be an exception. You can usually find it on sale for under $700, even with 16 GB of RAM and an OLED display.

According to recent reports, the OmniBook 5 isn’t quite as compact as the MacBook Neo because of its larger screen, but it is also half an inch thick and weighs only 2.8 pounds. The Snapdragon X Plus also delivers solid battery life, plenty to feel comfortable traveling with. It’s not a laptop without compromises (like the poor touchpad), but it comes with 16 GB of RAM, unlike some other laptops at this price. That’s a solid deal if you need something to travel with on a budget.

Good question. Tablets can make for great travel devices because of their size and ease of use. If you need a proper keyboard and touchpad—and the app support to handle a typical workday—you’re probably better off getting a laptop.

In a recent development, the Surface Pro 12 is the two-in-one laptop I’d recommend first. It’s absolutely tiny for a computer, even though it runs the full version of Windows 11. Even with the detachable keyboard connected, it weighs only 1.8 pounds. The only real problem with bringing this on a plane is the kickstand, which adds some extra depth. It’s just small enough that it should fit while open on an airplane tray table, unlike the 13.8-inch Surface Pro model.

Of course, that kickstand is also a huge advantage for the Surface Pro 12 if you’re using it without the keyboard. While that would make work difficult, it’s ideal for watching movies. Set this up on your tray table with some movies downloaded, and you’ll be the envy of your aisle. And when you need to get some work done in a coffee shop or at a smaller table, you’ll be happy to have access to the keyboard and touchpad—both of which are very comfortable to use. Just know that it's sold separately.

According to recent reports, the iPad Air, paired with the Magic Keyboard, avoids the Surface Pro 12’s kickstand concern. And with only an 11-inch screen, it’s perfect for use in small spaces—with or without the keyboard (note that there is also a 13-inch version). If you can accomplish all your work on an iPad, more power to ya! The iPad Air should give you everything you need, so long as you get the Magic Keyboard. If your travels involve more leisurely activities, the iPad Air is a great device for reading by the pool or for playing games.

One benefit of this latest version of the iPad Air is not only its performance (thanks to the M4 chip inside) but also the front-facing camera, which has been moved to landscape for more natural-feeling video calls. Of course, you could also opt for the 11-inch iPad Pro for extra performance (and the incredible tandem OLED screen). It’s also slightly thinner and lighter, though I don't think it's worth the significant price difference.

Industry observers note that lastly, there’s definitely room here for laptops with 360-degree hinges—a different class of two-in-one laptops. I haven’t tested a recent Windows device with this form factor that I truly loved, but there’s no question it works well on an airplane. Just fold the screen back with the keyboard face down, and you have the perfect screen for watching movies. The Lenovo Yoga 9i 14 is a gorgeous option, though it’s incredibly expensive right now. But if you can afford it, you’ll love the 2-in-1 action combined with one of the slickest designs imaginable. The Framework Laptop 12 is also worth considering. While it’s a bit thick and heavy for a travel laptop, its smaller screen, touchscreen, and 360-degree hinge make it a good option. It’s also one of the cheaper options available, and it’s user-upgradeable.

What to Look For in a Travel Laptop.

Recent findings suggest that whether you’re packing for a trip across the world or across the state, a proper travel laptop shouldn’t be heavy or overly large. That rules out 15-inch and 16-inch laptops, which are so substantial you can’t use them on airplane tray tables or at coffee shops. But even when you narrow it down to 14-inch laptops or smaller, there are three portability factors to consider.

When you’re on the go, you want a laptop that doesn’t constantly make you worry about finding an outlet. Bringing a laptop power bank can help, but the biggest factor in staying sane while traveling is a device that can stay on. Many factors affect how long a laptop can last, including CPU efficiency, battery wattage, screen brightness and resolution, and more.

Long-lasting laptops, such as the Dell XPS 13, will get you through a long flight. The processor is the main thing to look out for. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X series of chips are battery-efficient, as are Apple’s M-series chips. Intel also has some highly efficient CPUs in its most recent lineup, though you’ll need to pay close attention to the model number, as it can vary wildly depending on the specific CPU you’re using. To dig deeper, read my extensive guide on How to Buy the Right Laptop, which breaks down different CPU options.

How Large Are Airplane Tray Tables.

The size of seat-back tray tables varies. There’s no exact size because of various factors, such as the airline, aircraft, cabin, and seat. Remember: Just because a laptop can physically fit on a tray table doesn’t mean you’ll have space to open and use it. With that in mind, here are the general averages to keep in mind. Airlines do not list tray table sizes, but you can expect one in economy to measure around 16 x 9 inches, while premium cabins will have larger tables depending on the seat.

In a recent development, I’ve included both tablets and laptops in my recommendations, but your choice will depend on why you’re traveling with a device. If it’s for a vacation and you really only need a device to read, watch, and play on (perhaps with the occasional email check), a tablet works perfectly. Lounging with a tablet, whether on a plane or by the pool, feels much more leisurely than using a laptop. More importantly, it'll help you avoid dipping back into work mode. Whether an Android tablet, iPad, or Windows tablet, just pair it with a compatible keyboard case—and you’re good to go.

Recent findings suggest that however, if you’re traveling for work (or need to work while traveling), a proper laptop will be better. The one you already have may work just fine, but frequent fliers know they prefer a more compact device. And more specifically, a small laptop with a keyboard and trackpad will work better on your lap or on small desks than a tablet.

Sources indicate that the creator economy has exploded in recent years. TV reveals feature creators doing cameos as themselves, your favorite author is probably on BookTok, and Starbucks is paying baristas to make creator-style videos.

It has been revealed that at Mashable, we’re constantly covering what’s happening in the creator world, whether that’s at VidCon, the TikTok Awards, or in conversations across the internet. For our "Creator Playbook" series, we ask creators how they turn content into a career and about the tools they use to do so for "In My Bag.".

Industry observers note that in our inaugural Creators’ Choice Awards, we surveyed our favorite creators across the internet, including some of our Mashable 101 nominees. We wanted to know which gear and tools they use to see which brands and products are the most loved among digital creators. Now, we're ready to announce the winners.

A smartphone is the most basic tool a creator holds in their toolkit. Not only does it act as the camera, microphone, editor, and uploader, but it's also how they connect with followers.

In our own reporting, Senior Reporter Haley Henschel wrote, "For most of us, our phone is the most key device we own," calling it a "lifeline to friends" and "our primary gateway to the internet." She also noted that unless you carry around a separate camera, your phone is also how you document the world.

Phones are where people create and consume content. So, of course, we wanted to ask creators which phone brands they use and love.

Recent findings suggest that no surprise, our pool of creators overwhelmingly use Apple iPhones. They cited that they prefer Apple because the phones are easy to use and do everything they need from a mobile device. Most of our respondents had an iPhone 15 or newer.

“My entire life, business, and career [are] managed and created using my iPhone,” one respondent wrote.

Mashable's resident iPhone reviewer, Senior Editor Stan Schroeder, called all of the latest iPhones "blazing fast," and has lauded their cameras, battery life, and impressively fast performance in his reviews.

Some creators also commented on the phones’ long battery lives and impressive performance and features. One person remarked, “This phone is a workhorse,” while another called their iPhone “a power performer” that “gets everything you need done with a snap, with excellent battery life and storage.”.

In a recent development, we know that Apple loyalty runs deep, so we suspected it would hold the top spot among our surveyed creators. One even called themself “a forever customer of the brand.”.

Industry observers note that samsung Galaxy phones were a second favorite among our creator pool. Samsung stood out for its cameras and overall satisfaction with its phones. Per our reporting, Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra is "faster than some mid-range laptops we've tried," and the brand makes the best foldable Android phone.

Recent findings suggest that “It is the best phone available,” mentioned one respondent who has a Samsung Galaxy S26+. Another creator agreed that “Samsung makes the best phones, period.”.

Survey respondents praised Samsung’s operating system, processor, AI integration, and long battery life.

“I do the majority of my content creation on my phone and find it very easy to use,” one creator noted.

Sources indicate that while a phone might be the most accessible or most-used tool for content creation, some creators take video editing or design work to their personal computers. Henschel writes, "The best laptops are fast enough for their primary use cases, well-made, and priced fairly for their specs." We were curious which machines power our favorite creators’ content, and the results were pretty split among different brands.

Though, our creators did choose laptop brands that Mashable experts personally recommend.

Apple reigned supreme as the most preferred laptop brand for our survey takers. They like MacBooks for their compatibility with other Apple devices, sleek design, and overall usability.

Industry observers note that "It looks nice and it works for so many things," one respondent wrote. "There is nothing you can't do on it — it's definitely worth the price.".

Creators also reported that the software they use to create their content runs well on Apple laptops and that the MacBooks are fast.

It has been revealed that one creator wrote, “As a musician, I love the MacBook Pro because of its capabilities for creating music and music content. I frequently run Logic Pro and MuseScore on my MacBook to create music, both of which run super smoothly. I also use it to edit videos featuring my music for social media. I would definitely recommend this computer to another musician.”.

Another mentioned their MacBook is “very capable” of doing what they need when putting together content.

Industry observers note that apple’s laptops are definitely a favorite for creatives. “It's great for everything you need as a content creator,” wrote one respondent.

Sources indicate that our creators also prefer Dell for their computing needs. Multiple people noted the longevity of their Dell laptops, with one noting that they’ve had theirs for more than 10 years.

Respondents said simply, “I love my Dell,” and “It’s my favorite.”.

Other comments praised Dell’s processing speed, RAM capacity, battery life, ease of use, and durability. These same qualities are why you'll find multiple Dell computers on our list of the best Windows laptops.

Recent findings suggest that participants in our Creators’ Choice survey also preferred Microsoft laptops. They lauded the laptops' speed, processor, and design, with one person commenting specifically on how easy it is for them to create and edit vlogs.

One creator put it simply: “It's an all-rounder and is good for most people.”.

According to recent reports, the final winner in the laptop category is HP. Creators love the brand’s laptops for their speed, quality, and affordability.

“My HP laptop is fast, reliable, and handles everyday tasks with ease,” wrote one participant, adding that it’s actually a great value for its price.

Others noted HP’s ease in multitasking and the power behind its laptops. One creator said, “It is easy to use, affordable, durable, and can be used for many things such as recording, video calls, and editing pictures.”.

While video is arguably the most popular medium for creators in 2026, many still use photo-editing tools and incorporate photography into their feeds.

Sources indicate that adobe reigns supreme in editing tools for our creators, including its photo-centric tools like Photoshop and Lightroom. Many respondents praised Adobe apps’ ease of use and their editing tools for both professionals and hobbyists.

Multiple people said Adobe is their “go-to” editing tool and that it’s “the best I’ve ever used.”.

Sources indicate that “This photo editing software is amazing, and I swear by it,” wrote a survey respondent. “The results speak for themselves.”.

One person mentioned that Adobe’s AI features “make editing so much more efficient” and that they’d recommend it based on that alone.

The second-most preferred photo editing tool among our survey pool is Canva. Creators love that it’s accessible and easy to use, even for non-professionals.

One comment stated, “I like that it's free to use and still has good editing tools for free users.”.

Videos make up the majority of creator-made content on social media, whether on TikTok, Instagram Reels, or YouTube, and our creators have two favorite video editing brands.

Industry observers note that adobe was their top choice again, with a large number of responses noting how easy the programs are to use. One creator called Adobe Premiere “an amazing software,” while another mentioned it’s “perfect for what I need it for.”.

Others commented on Adobe being a great editing platform and having a good variety of editing tools.

Another favorite video editing tool among our creator pool is CapCut. The mobile-first editing program is incredibly easy to use, according to our respondents. They also like it for its TikTok integration.

One respondent who claims they’ve been an avid CapCut user before it was even called CapCut wrote, “It’s been the best editing software I’ve ever used.”.

Affordability is another area where CapCut shines — one creator called it “a steal.”.

Graphic design can enhance your content with stronger visuals or allow you to create recognizable branding.

Recent findings suggest that and, once again, Adobe was a favorite for our creators. They prefer it for its ease of use and breadth of tools.

One creator said Adobe has a “great comprehensive suite of design and editing tools that are crucial to making the best content.”.

Another called Adobe the “best in the business.”.

Canva was another top choice in our survey results. People prefer it because it’s also very easy to use and free or affordable.

“I like Canva because it has great tools that make editing more fun,” wrote one respondent.

Another remarked, “It can do lots of different things to make great products.”.

It has been revealed that though smartphones have pretty stellar onboard cameras, many creators still opt for a dedicated vlogging camera. You'll find an array of cameras featured in our In My Bag series, but these are the top three brands, according to the creators who took our survey.

Canon was the favorite camera brand among the survey pool. They praised Canon cameras’ great quality and durability. One person mentioned their Canon PowerShot G7 X “has been a great camera that lasted through the years.”.

Creators from our survey also use and like Sony vlogging cameras. They recommend Sony cameras for beginners and pros alike. One respondent remarked, “I recommend them because they have very good quality; they are certainly very good investments.”.

Creators also like Panasonic for its audio quality, image quality, battery life, and user-friendliness.

Sources indicate that while we had creators answering questions about their favorite tools and gear, we, of course, also had to ask them about which social media platform they use the most. Drumroll please….

Facebook actually came out on top as the most-used social media among our respondents.

Recent findings suggest that they like Facebook mostly for personal use and keeping up with friends and family members. Many people remarked the platform is great for connecting with others.

“I have been using it for years and is the best way i have found to stay in touch with people and share my story,” mentioned one respondent.

It has been revealed that on the subject of using Facebook for years, one person called it “the O.G. of social media,” adding that “there is nothing not to like” about it.

According to recent reports, another Meta platform was also a favorite: Creators like Instagram for how easy it is to use and for connecting with friends and followers. According to one creator, “it offers a visually engaging platform to connect with friends, family, and global communities.”.

Others praised the creativity and engagement of the platform, shouting out its wide array of content types.

One of the creators said, “I love using Instagram,” calling it “one of the best social platforms around.”.

The next most-used social media platform is TikTok. Many of the creators we talk to and write about use TikTok as their main platform. Our survey group likes TikTok for its large audience, universal appeal, and fun content.

According to one respondent, it’s the best place to get a start on social media. Once you’ve gotten that start, one creator stated, “It's a good platform for people who want to share their life or creations through short-form videos. Or if they want to post short clips from their longer videos to attract viewers to their YouTube channel.”.

And that brings us to our creator pool's final favorite social media platform: YouTube. Similar to TikTok, one creator mentioned, “It's a great place to post your content, whether long or short form, and is used by millions.”.

Others love it for the easy-to-use platform and quality features, calling it “fun and cool” and “better than the other brands.”.

Europe is entering a ‘supercycle’ of national elections. Their outcomes could shake the EU’s foundations

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1283 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As nationalist, Eurosceptic parties surge in four of the bloc’s biggest member states, the coming year’s polls could test its resilience like never before.
  • In late 1998, Tony Blair was prime minister of Britain, Lionel Jospin was prime minister of France, and Gerhard Schröder had just been elected chancellor of Germany.
  • In a recent development, brisk economic growth was lifting living standards.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As nationalist, Eurosceptic parties surge in four of the bloc’s biggest member states, the coming year’s polls could test its resilience like never before.

In late 1998, Tony Blair was prime minister of Britain, Lionel Jospin was prime minister of France, and Gerhard Schröder had just been elected chancellor of Germany. The EU had 15 member states and pro-European, centre-left parties were in power – either alone or in coalitions – in all but two of them.

In a recent development, brisk economic growth was lifting living standards. Eastward enlargement was under way. In Washington, Bill Clinton was pursuing the same brand of “third way” centrism as a middle path between free-market capitalism and traditional socialism. The EU felt like it had the tide of history behind it.

Not quite three decades later, the continent’s politics once again seem to be tilting in a single direction – except this time, the momentum belongs to the nationalist far right, and the outcome could be a significant unpicking of the postwar European consensus that built the EU.

Between the end of this month and the end of next year, an extraordinary electoral sequence will sweep the bloc. Voters in four of the EU’s five biggest member states, by population and economy, head to the polls, with parliamentary elections also due in Estonia, Finland, Greece and Slovakia, and regional ballots in Germany.

Spain kicks off the cycle with a snap general election on 29 November, with prime minister Pedro Sánchez’s socialist coalition facing probable defeat to rightwing parties in the shape of the conservative People’s party (PP) and far-right Vox, which already govern together in some Spanish regions.

Next come presidential and parliamentary elections in France in the spring. The clear frontrunner in the presidential race is Marine Le Pen of far-right the National Rally (RN), well ahead of the far-left firebrand Jean-Luc Mélenchon and a hopelessly divided mainstream opposition.

In a recent development, when Poland votes later next year, nationalist parties that between them command nearly half the national vote could well unseat the liberal coalition of prime minister, Donald Tusk, despite recent splits. And in Italy, Giorgia Meloni, whose Brothers of Italy party has far-right roots, hopes to secure a second term in elections due before the end of 2027 – while facing pressure on her right flank from the upstart National Future party.

According to recent reports, paradoxically, this nationalist surge arrives amid strong public support for the EU. Shocked by the chaos of Brexit and seeking reassurance in an increasingly alarming world, a record 74% of Europeans say their country benefits from membership, and very few Eurosceptic parties now advocate leaving outright.

It has been revealed that the Eurosceptics and nationalists do, however, still view the bloc as a top-down project that undermines national sovereignty, and aim to transform it into an altogether looser association of sovereign nation-states. In the words of the Italian political scientist Natalie Tocci, that means this coming electoral supercycle could “dramatically change the face of Europe” – triggering not simply “a slow erosion of the European project but a hollowing out, if not an outright implosion”.

Industry observers note that all elections differ and national specifics loom large. But analysts agree the underlying forces at work here are connected: sluggish growth, ageing populations, strained public finances and a spiralling cost of living have chipped away at support for Europe’s traditional catch-all centre-left and centre-right parties. The wave of youth-led protests sweeping Europe is only the most visible sign of deep voter discontent.

Meanwhile, nationalist parties have become increasingly adept at conjuring and exploiting an ever-evolving list of supposed threats and crises, from migration and vaccines to the green transition, support for Ukraine, globalisation, international elites and supranational institutions – narratives bolstered by Russian disinformation and overt backing for “patriotic” parties from Donald Trump’s White House. As a result, politics has fragmented, and polarised: nearly one in four voters now backs far-right parties – a share that has grown almost fivefold since the mid-1990s.

The rise has not been linear: over the past year or so, while the far-right Alternative für Deutschland scored a historic regional election victory in eastern Germany, in the Netherlands Geert Wilders’s Freedom party lost nearly a third of its seats, Viktor Orbán’s Fidesz was soundly beaten in Hungary and the far-right Sweden Democrats shed support for the first time in 16 years.

But the underlying upward trend appears clear – fuelled above all, political scientists argue, by the normalisation and mainstreaming of far-right ideas, most notably on immigration. Centre-right parties are gradually dismantling “firewalls” that once barred cooperation with the radical right. At the European level, the centre-right European People’s party has increasingly turned to farther-right groups to roll back parts of the European green deal and tighten migration rules.

In a recent development, for the EU, the biggest impact of this election supercycle could be in the European Council of national leaders, which now features just three centre-left heads of government out of 27. If Eurosceptic leaders in France, Spain and Poland join those of Czechia, Italy, Romania, Slovakia and Slovenia by the end of 2027, they would not have the numbers to rewrite EU law – but they would constitute a formidable blocking minority.

EU budget negotiations, future enlargement, aid to Ukraine and deeper integration in essential fields such as defence, energy, finance and technology could all face paralysis, analysts warn.

Safety in numbers, notes Tocci, could change current leaders’ behaviour in the council. Meloni’s relative restraint has been dictated, in part, by her relative isolation among mainstream peers such as Tusk, Sánchez and France’s Emmanuel Macron (alongside Rome’s reliance on €200bn in EU recovery funds).

If she were instead sitting down with the likes of Le Pen, Poland’s far-right Law and Justice (PiS) leader, Jarosław Kaczyński, and a Vox-backed Spanish government, with National Future’s hardline Roberto Vannacci breathing down her neck at home and those EU funds winding down, she might have less incentive to play pro-EU ball.

Sources indicate that analysts agree, though, that the decisive battleground is France. Le Pen’s election platform sets her on a collision course with Brussels: she aims to cut €11bn from France’s EU budget contribution, hold a constitutional referendum to proclaim the supremacy of French over European law, and breach various single-market rules.

In a recent development, and France “carries very significant influence over the EU”, noted Mujtaba Rahman of the Eurasia Group consultancy. Compared with Orbán, he notes, a president Le Pen would have “far more leverage to carry out the far-right playbook of subverting the EU’s law-based, supranational architecture”.

It has been revealed that until now, Brussels has contained disruptors such as Orbán largely because there were rarely more than two or three round the table. A cohesive Eurosceptic bloc would leave the EU unable to enforce rule-of-law standards, further integrate economic and security policies or, indeed, agree on anything much at all. The first victim would very probably be Ukraine, with Le Pen leading a blocking caucus against further aid.

Three decades on from 1998, Europe’s coming elections, concluded Stefan Lehne of the Carnegie Europe thinktank, could well turn into “key tests of the EU’s resilience”. The threat to the bloc might not be immediate or existential, he said, but the medium-term risks were significant.

Sources indicate that “A stronger role for the radical right may be unlikely to dismantle the EU as it exists today,” Lehne said, but could “prevent it from becoming what it needs to be to deal with the challenges of the future”. And gradually but inevitably, prolonged failure to act collectively as and where needed would lead a “loss of relevance”.

What a billion-dollar deal claims about the US battery market

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (664 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Technologyreview

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After a tough few years littered with some high-profile failures, there’s some positive news for next-generation batteries in the US.
  • Sila just signed an agreement with Panasonic Energy, a global battery manufacturer, to supply silicon-carbon anode material, a possible key to smaller, lighter batteries.
  • According to recent reports, this arrangement also demonstrates how much the politics of batteries have shifted lately.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a tough few years littered with some high-profile failures, there’s some positive news for next-generation batteries in the US.

Sila just signed an agreement with Panasonic Energy, a global battery manufacturer, to supply silicon-carbon anode material, a possible key to smaller, lighter batteries. It’s a deal that Sila says could be worth more than $1 billion over time.

According to recent reports, this arrangement also demonstrates how much the politics of batteries have shifted lately. A major part of the financial backing for this factory’s production is a $1.4 billion loan from the Trump administration’s Defense Department. While batteries can be a major tool to help drive the energy transition and cut emissions, right now much of the industry is more focused on geopolitics.

According to recent reports, founded in 2011, Sila makes silicon-based anodes for lithium-ion batteries. The major selling point here is the potential to improve energy density—Sila’s anode weighs a fifth as much as the graphite used in anodes today and cuts the volume in half, according to the manufacturer. So using this new material enables batteries to pack more energy into the same weight and volume, allowing longer range for EVs, for example. The material can also deliver more power and recharge faster, compared with conventional chemistry.

It has been revealed that we’ve been following Sila (and its competitors) for years. My colleague James Temple covered the manufacturer when its battery first appeared in Whoop fitness wearables in 2021.

Things have gotten a lot bigger since then. In 2022, Sila unveiled looks for a factory in Moses Lake, Washington, and received $100 million from the US Department of Energy, part of a multibillion-dollar round of grants under the Biden administration to support the US battery supply chain.

The firm opened its factory in September 2025, and it’s already operating. But the deal with Panasonic will help it scale to at least 10 times more production than current levels, claims Gene Berdichevsky, the company’s cofounder and CEO.

Panasonic has committed to buying tens of thousands of tons of material, Berdichevsky claims, though Sila isn’t sharing specific numbers on the total commitment or the price Panasonic is paying.

Industry observers note that this agreement is Sila’s first mass-market deal and a big one for the United States’ next-generation battery market, which has largely been on the ropes over the past few years. Two billion-dollar battery companies, 24M and ESS Tech, have declared bankruptcy and shut down just in the last year.

According to recent reports, the glimmer of hope here is tied up with something I’ve been noticing about this industry: the shifting politics. While batteries used to be firmly considered a climate technology, we’ve seen a lot of companies move away from messaging around the clean energy transition and lean into geopolitics.

Industry observers note that china dominates the battery world and particularly the battery anode market, controlling over 90% of graphite production today. For years, the US has been trying to curb reliance on Chinese batteries, battery materials, and other materials used in crucial technologies, like rare earth metals. But the Trump administration has ramped things up, and earlier this year the US Defense Department committed a $1.4 billion loan to Sila aimed at helping the US face a “significant technology sovereignty challenge,” as a press release put it.

Sila’s announcement of the Panasonic deal does mention EVs—but not climate, emissions or the energy transition. Rather, it’s all about American industrialization. (And, of course, a mention that a North American battery supply chain can also help power the AI market.).

I asked Berdichevsky about this shift and whether the manufacturer holds decarbonization as a priority.

In a recent development, “I think the politics of it has shifted around us much more than our motivations have shifted,” he said. “It’s really the energy efficiency that motivates engineers like myself and technologists at our manufacturer. And I still think that that’s still at the heart of it.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Employees at Foundation Future Industries were told that their health benefits through administrator Rippling have been terminated, according to a memo obtained by CNBC, adding to mounting signs of financial distress at the humanoid robot startup advised and backed by Eric Trump.
  • Foundation told staff in a Friday evening email that they'd be offered coverage through COBRA, the federal law that generally lets workers temporarily keep their health insurance after losing benefits by paying the full premium out of pocket.
  • "Because our last pay run through Rippling was in October, they have ended our benefits with them retroactive to October," a Foundation human resources manager mentioned in the memo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Employees at Foundation Future Industries were told that their health benefits through administrator Rippling have been terminated, according to a memo obtained by CNBC, adding to mounting signs of financial distress at the humanoid robot startup advised and backed by Eric Trump.

Foundation told staff in a Friday evening email that they'd be offered coverage through COBRA, the federal law that generally lets workers temporarily keep their health insurance after losing benefits by paying the full premium out of pocket.

"Because our last pay run through Rippling was in October, they have ended our benefits with them retroactive to October," a Foundation human resources manager mentioned in the memo. "COBRA will be offered to all employees to cover November.".

In a recent development, foundation has garnered headlines for the bold claims that co-founder Sankaet Pathak — whose previous startup collapsed in 2024 — has made about his robots and their potential use in war zones. Employees were last paid on Oct. 15, and some inside the organization are angry at Pathak for a $4.6 million loan he took from his company last year, CNBC reported earlier this month.

A Foundation spokesman didn't immediately respond to an email or phone call seeking comment.

Sources indicate that in the staff memo, Foundation blamed Rippling for the disruption to health coverage. The startup also remarked it would reimburse COBRA premiums paid by workers and that it was onboarding a fresh benefits provider.

But employees, especially those whose family members are undergoing treatment for medical ailments, worry the manufacturer won't have funds to reimburse workers or reinstate coverage, people with direct knowledge of the situation said.

In a statement to CNBC, Rippling indicated it was Foundation's failure to pay for its employee benefits that led to the change: "If a client enrolled in Rippling's [Professional Employer Organization] is unable to meet their payroll and benefits obligations for multiple months, they will first receive a warning and if not met, they are terminated.".

Recent findings suggest that foundation has been seeking a bridge loan to repay employees after its financial woes began in August. It has been in talks with three or four venture capital firms, including existing investor Tribe Capital, Pathak has told employees, according to people familiar with the situation, who asked to remain unnamed because they were not authorized to speak publicly and feared retaliation. Tribe didn't immediately return a request for comment.

The bridge loan would help the organization survive until a possible $150 million investment from South Korean conglomerate Base Group lands as early as December or January, Pathak has told employees, the people said.

Base confirmed to Reuters in recent days that it was considering an investment, but the funding has not been finalized.

The potential investment would deepen business ties between the Trump family and the South Korean conglomerate, an aluminum producer also known for real estate and hospitality projects.

Base paid the Trump Organization $2 million in 2025, according to a Upcoming York Times article, drawing scrutiny from Democratic senators over conflict-of-interest concerns. Base has also pursued other business relationships with the Trump Organization, including a Trump-branded golf course in South Korea.

Eric Trump, who has invested in Foundation and was given the title of chief strategy advisor, didn't immediately respond to a CNBC email seeking comment.

The prospect of employees having to pay for their own health coverage comes as many are already drawing down savings to cover living expenses. With another scheduled payday approaching on Nov. 30, workers are facing a third straight pay cycle without income.

Many are actively interviewing for other jobs, and attendance at the manufacturer's San Francisco headquarters has fallen sharply, according to people familiar.

Frustration has boiled over into distrust of Pathak's leadership for some employees, while others hope Pathak can secure funding to repay workers and bring the organization back to financial health. In conversations and memos, Pathak indicates that he is highly invested in securing Foundation's future, the people said.

Despite the firm's shaky finances, Foundation continued to hire for open roles until recently and some new workers have never been fully paid, said the people.

To keep employees from leaving before a possible Base Group investment, Pathak has floated the idea of offering workers equity in the startup, the people noted.

At the same time, human resources staff have warned workers against taking legal action with California to recover their wages, saying that any employees who file complaints with the state would be dismissed, the people said.

Sources indicate that following a Nov. 14 CNBC report detailing the missed payrolls and a $4.6 million loan Pathak took from the startup in 2025, the chief executive addressed the issue in an all-hands meeting, according to the people.

Pathak defended the arrangement by telling workers that he had plowed his own money into the startup and takes only a nominal salary, the people noted.

The co-founder also told employees who were in dire financial straits to contact human resources for help covering personal bills, the people added.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm burning through savings just to afford my apartment," one employee told CNBC. "It's extremely unfortunate we're in this situation.".

#127589. A human liver has been kept alive outside the body for a record seven weeks

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1036 w)
